summary: Travis Frisinger, technical director of AI ETHLite, presents a top-down theory of why LLMs perform well despite lacking intelligence, intent, or desire. He traces his journey chronologically: GPT-3.5's brittleness in November 2022 gave way to GPT-4's uncanny fluency in January 2023, which he explored through live-streamed pair programming, building Webcat, co-authoring AIBuddy.software, and producing a feline metal concept album. Analyzing his ChatGPT history yielded the AI Decision Loop (frame, generate, judge, validate, iterate, simplified to frame, generate, judge, iterate), where most people fail at the judge stage. He then formulates coherence theory, drawing on Anthropic's feature superposition and concept circuits research. Coherence has four properties: relevance (output feels topical), consistency (maintains tone and terminology across turns), stability (withstands interrogation and pressure), and emergence (abilities like diagnosing swine disease or cancer patterns without specific training). Meaning is not retrieved but constructed on demand from distributed sparks across neurons in superposition. Prompts act as force vectors navigating high-dimensional latent space, lighting up specialized subnetworks that merge into new ideas at inference time. He proposes a three-layer model: latent space (internal structure), execution layer (tools, APIs, retrieval), and conversational interface (human intent). Engineering implications include treating hallucinations as coherence indicators rather than bugs, using RAG as factual anchors providing contextual gravity, designing for emergence rather than control, keeping reasoning chains modular, and watching for tone or structure breakdowns as early warning signs. He concludes that LLMs are high-dimensional mirrors resonating through structure, not thinkers—coherent, not intelligent—and that is their superpower.

sections.title: Introduction and the Coherency Trap
sections.summary: Frisinger introduces himself as technical director of AI ETHLite and frames the talk as a top-down exploration of why LLMs work well despite lacking intelligence, intent, or desire. It is a story of chasing a feeling across experiments, analysis, and theory formulation.

sections.title: From GPT-3.5 Disappointment to GPT-4 Uncanny
sections.summary: He recounts his November 2022 disappointment with GPT-3.5's brittleness, prompt sensitivity, and context limits. GPT-4 in January 2023 produced an uncanny experience of effortless alignment, paralleling Microsoft's Sparks of AGI paper and Ethan Mollick's research. He felt an intermediate space between dumb chatbots and AGI existed that needed exploration.

sections.title: Early Experiments: Live Streaming and Webcat
sections.summary: He began live-streaming paired programming sessions with ChatGPT, producing a few hundred lines of usable code. He built Webcat, a Python Azure function for scraping web pages, to compensate for early ChatGPT-4's lack of internet access. These became prototypes for AI pair programming techniques still used today in tools like Cursor and Windsurf.

sections.title: Creative Collaboration: Blog and Feline Metal Album
sections.summary: He collaboratively built AIBuddy.software with AI, letting it pick the Ghost platform. He then produced a feline metal concept album using ChatGPT for lyrics, composition, and image editing, gaining over 3,000 views in a month with positive reception, demonstrating coherent creative value beyond his solo capabilities.

sections.title: AI Decision Loop Framework
sections.summary: He built an analysis tool to examine his ChatGPT history for decision intelligence and pairing behaviors, resulting in a 21-page case study. He derived the AI Decision Loop: frame, generate, judge, validate, iterate, simplified to frame, generate, judge, iterate. Most people fail by not critically engaging with and evaluating output.

sections.title: Coherence Theory Introduction
sections.summary: Drawing on NLP experience and Anthropic's work on feature superposition and concept circuits, he proposes coherence as a system property rather than a cognitive one. It is precognitive, serving as the infrastructure that thought navigates, offering a framework to explain LLM behavior without invoking true thinking.

sections.title: Coherence Properties and Superposition Mechanics
sections.summary: Frisinger defines coherence's four properties: relevance (topical output), consistency (maintained tone and terminology across turns), stability (withstanding interrogation without collapsing), and emergence (untrained capabilities like disease diagnosis via coherent pattern alignment). He explains superposition: concepts are distributed across neurons that can hold multiple ideas, meaning is constructed on demand, not retrieved.

sections.title: Prompts as Force Vectors in Latent Space
sections.summary: He reframes prompts as force vectors with directional force in high-dimensional latent space. Context lights up specialized conceptual clouds at inference time, merging subnetworks into new ideas. He cites Anthropic, Ethan Mollick, and Stanford CRFM as supporting research. LLM utility lies in essence reconstruction—creating new ideas from multiple essences—not compression and retrieval.

sections.title: Engineering for Coherence Not Intelligence
sections.summary: He presents engineering implications: hallucinations are coherence indicators (features, not bugs) that fill gaps predictably. RAG fragments serve as factual anchors with contextual gravity. He introduces a three-layer model: latent space, execution layer (tools, APIs, retrieval), and conversational interface (human intent). Prompts are interfaces, not one-offs. Design for emergence, keep chains modular, watch for tone and structure breakdowns as early warning signs.

sections.title: LLMs as High-Dimensional Mirrors
sections.summary: He concludes that LLMs are high-dimensional mirrors with 80,000+ dimensions. The machine doesn't understand you; it resonates through structure, not thought. Sometimes reflections are sharper than the input. LLMs are coherent, not intelligent—and that is their superpower. Stop chasing intelligence and start designing for structured resonance.
